acceptance.criterion_verbatim: EACH TABLE IS STILL READABLE AND WRITABLE ON THE DATA PLANE, WHICH `describe-table` CANNOT SHOW: per table, a fixture item written and read back after the flip, then deleted and the deletion read back. A control-plane read reporting the new key ARN is NOT this criterion -- it shows what the key is configured as, never that the table can still be used. NEGATIVE CONTROL: state what a failure would have looked like (an `AccessDeniedException` or `KMSInvalidStateException` on the data-plane call) so a clean pass is distinguishable from an unexercised one.
acceptance.invocation: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name opal-users-v2 --item '{"PK":{"S":"FIXTURE#opsec-s8r2b-cmk-verify"},"SK":{"S":"PROBE#20260903T235458Z"},...}' --return-consumed-capacity TOTAL ; aws dynamodb get-item --consistent-read ; aws dynamodb delete-item --return-values ALL_OLD ; aws dynamodb get-item --consistent-read
acceptance.output_evidence: FOUR STEPS, ALL ON THE DATA PLANE. (1) WRITE, the encrypt path on the new CMK: put-item returned {"ConsumedCapacity":{"TableName":"opal-users-v2","CapacityUnits":1.0}}. (2) READ BACK, the decrypt path, with --consistent-read so the row came from storage and not a cache: returned the item byte-exact -- PK FIXTURE#opsec-s8r2b-cmk-verify, SK PROBE#20260903T235458Z, purpose 'TO-OP-S-8R2B S8B-AC3 data-plane exercise; delete immediately'. (3) DELETE with --return-values ALL_OLD returned the full item, proving it existed and was removed. (4) CLEANUP READ BACK with --consistent-read returned an empty response with NO Item key; a later re-read is likewise empty, so no fixture residue remains and ItemCount is back to 75. NEGATIVE CONTROL, STATED: a failure would have surfaced as AccessDeniedException or KMSInvalidStateException on the write or on the consistent read. Neither occurred. The CONSISTENT READ is the discriminating leg -- an unusable key cannot decrypt, so DynamoDB would have errored rather than returning the row; a table that were encrypted-but-unreadable fails exactly there and nowhere else in this face. SECOND INSTRUMENT ON A DIFFERENT PLANE, so this is corroboration and not one instrument read twice: aws kms list-grants --key-id 64f25291-... returns a grant with GranteePrincipal dynamodb.us-east-1.amazonaws.com whose Name is 8e590a34-53b1-4b6a-8c91-02bbc5e981ea -- opal-users-v2's own TableId -- and EncryptionContextSubset {"aws:dynamodb:tableName":"opal-users-v2","aws:dynamodb:subscriberId":"313476888478"}, granting Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey/ReEncryptFrom/ReEncryptTo/RetireGrant/DescribeKey. DynamoDB minted that grant because the table now uses this key.
